name: lane-book-{DAY}
title: Lane book {DAY}
subtitle: The month's road: lanes of opportunity, each one SQL condition tested on the panel store's history and read on today's names, beside the dated catalysts by week, value against catalyst timing (when a discount pays), industry rotation with its record, the Book and the cash above the floor. Every column is its own read; nothing is a sum.
sources_extra: lanes, names, when_value, rotation, timeline: {PACK}/lane_book (tv_scan_cli.py lane-book; recipe config/generic_utils/lane_book.json)

guide.intro: The lane book answers: which kinds of trade have paid on this store, which names are in them today, when in the catalyst cycle a discount pays, and where the month's dated events fall. Tables are data from tv_scan_cli.py lane-book; the Month plan, Course / Reason and every callout are judgment. A lane's record is in-sample on one regime: read n, days, the halves and the months before trusting a mean.

The read and critical callouts, then the road.

Each lane by month of entry: one good month is one episode.
The two charts, then a lane's screen.

The weeks table, then This week / Next week + Lane names.

Each held line's lanes, cell and levels.

sections.title: Reading rules
rows: Read xs against the base row, not against 0.
Mean excess over a median is positive for every name (returns are skewed): the base lane's xs_28 is the zero line.
Trust a lane only when t, both halves and most months agree.
Windows overlap; t uses calendar blocks of h days, the halves split the store in time.
p_up / p_dn are raw odds of a 10% move.
They answer 'can this make 10%+ in a month' directly; the base is about 19% up and 16% down.
A name's best lane is the lane's record, not the name's forecast.
Lanes overlap: the best measured lane is one read, never a sum of lanes.
Value pays at a time: read the When tab before buying a discount.
The discount's edge moves with the distance to the print.
OUTSIDE news changes timing or grade only.
It never reorders a table or sizes a ticket.
The lane's key in config/generic_utils/lane_book.json (one SQL condition on the store's features).
long = read as a buy; avoid = read as what not to chase (a short-side read); base = every name, the zero line.
The lane's kind: quality / value, moves, trend, catalyst, flow, AI lane, base.
The lane's SQL condition on the store's features (macros expanded on the store, shown as written in the recipe).
all = every floor name; ai = the AI / data-center cluster (ai_buildout industries, hyperscalers); other = the rest; strong / weak = business-quality splits on the When tab.
Rows (name-days) with a 7 / 14 / 28-day label in the cell.
Store days with at least one row in the cell.
Distinct names (or industries on the rotation table) in the cell.
All rows in the cell, labelled or not.
Mean raw return over the next 7 / 14 / 28 calendar days, %, clipped at the recipe's clip_pct.
Median raw return over the next 7 / 14 / 28 days, %.
Mean excess return over the next 7 / 14 / 28 days: the name's return minus that day's median floor name, pp. Read against the base row (about +0.6 at 28 days), not against 0.
Share of rows that beat that day's median floor name, %.
Odds of a raw rise of 10% or more inside 7 / 14 / 28 days, % of rows.
Odds of a raw fall of 10% or more inside 7 / 14 / 28 days, % of rows.
t of the excess across calendar blocks of h days (daily cell means averaged per block; the blocks are the independent pieces). 2+ = consistent across blocks.
Calendar blocks of h days behind t.
Mean excess in the store's first half of labelled days.
Mean excess in the store's second half of labelled days.
Names in the lane on the newest store day.
The first names in the lane today, in the lane's recipe order.
Month of entry (the store day the row starts).
Every name on the floor (the base rate) (base): What the average US $2B+ name did: every lane is read against this row.
Quality repairing from depth (long): FCF margin 10%+, estimates not cut, net debt under 2x EBITDA, and under the 200-day or 30%+ under the high: the 11 Nov mover study's edge, without a move trigger.
Quality from depth, turning (week +5%) (long): The same quality-from-depth names once the week turns up 5%+: the repair with price confirmation.
Quality from depth after a +7% day (long): The mover-study cell (a big up day on a strong, deep name); thin, read its n.
Quality uptrend back at the 50-day (long): Strong names in an uptrend that pulled back to their 50-day: buy-the-dip inside a trend.
Cheaper than peers, estimates up, turning up (long): Forward earnings yield 2+ points over the industry median, estimates rising, still under the 50-day but up on the week.
Estimates up 5%+, price down on the month (long): The street raised next-year EPS 5%+ over 3 months while the price fell: revisions the tape has not paid.
Street 30%+ over, estimates not cut, cash positive, 25%+ under the high (long): A deep drawdown the street still prices 30%+ higher, with estimates intact and cash coming in.
Quality washed out (RSI 35 or under) (long): Strong businesses at an oversold RSI: the washed-out entry.

Low bar into the print (sold into it, last print sold, revisions not crowded) (long): The signal lab's best pre-print cell on the store: price down into the print, the last print sold off, revisions under the crowded top quintile.
Build-up: strong and cheaper than peers, print in 8-28 days (long): Quality cheaper than its industry with a print three to four weeks out: bought before the event, not chased after it.
Beat both and gapped up 3%+ (post-print drift) (long): Printed in the last 3 days, beat EPS and revenue, the reaction day closed up 3%+.
Beat both, sold 3%+ on the print (long): A beat on both lines that the market sold: the dip after a good print.

Moving without a print (week +4%, volume up, cheaper than peers) (long): Up 4%+ on the week on above-average volume with no print in 10 days or the next 5, cheaper than peers: buying without a catalyst.
AI cluster quality 20%+ under the high (long): The AI / data-center cluster's strong names after the drawdown: the contagion lane, read with the cluster triggers.
Any +7% day (chasing the move) (avoid): The base for chasing: what a +7% day did next, any name.
Momentum at the high (within 5%, estimates +10%, 3 months +30%) (avoid): The crowded winner: near the high with estimates and price both already up a lot.
Big mover the continuation score likes (top fifth) (avoid): A big move the move-prediction continuation score ranks in its top fifth.
Cash burner after a big move (avoid): A +7% day or +15% week on a business with negative free cash flow.
Rich to peers, up 10%+ on the month into a print within 10 days (avoid): Priced over its industry and run up into the print: the sell-the-news set-up.
Estimates cut 5%+, under the 200-day, month down (avoid): The falling knife: the business and the price going down together (short-side reading).
